en: to be accumulated; to build up

examples.en: Fatigue builds up in the body.
When long experience accumulates, your skill grows.
Knowledge does not accumulate overnight.
The more data accumulates, the more accurate the results get.
Heat has built up in the room, so it is hot.

examples.ko: 이 기술은 수십 년 동안 축적된 노력의 결과예요.
examples.en: This technology is the result of effort accumulated over decades.

explain: '쌓이다'보다 딱딱한 말로, 경험·지식·자료·피로처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에 자주 써요. 먼지나 눈처럼 눈에 보이는 것은 '쌓이다'가 더 자연스러워요. 사람이 모으는 쪽은 '축적하다'예요.

phrases.en: If you work for a long time, experience accumulates.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 안 보이는 경험이 쌓일 때 '축적되다'를 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 축적되다 is often used for invisible things like experience that build up.

phrases.en: The more you read, the more knowledge accumulates.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지식이나 자료가 차곡차곡 쌓이는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It conveys knowledge or data piling up steadily.

phrases.example: 이 박물관에는 오래된 자료가 많이 축적되어 있어요.
phrases.en: A lot of old material has been accumulated in this museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쌓여서 지금 그 상태로 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means things have built up and are in that state now.

explain_en: Knowledge, wealth or fatigue gathers gradually — written. A stiffer word than '쌓이다', often used for invisible things like experience, knowledge, data and fatigue. For visible things like dust or snow, '쌓이다' sounds more natural. The person-does-it form is '축적하다'.

t90.ax: Fatigue builds up in the body.

examples.en: The kids learned the breaststroke first at the pool.
I'm good at the breaststroke, but freestyle is hard for me.
I moved slowly forward doing the breaststroke.

examples.ko: 동생이 개구리헤엄으로 수영장 한 바퀴를 돌았어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling swam one lap of the pool with the breaststroke.
Try stretching your legs out straight like in the breaststroke.
The breaststroke looks easy, but the breathing is hard.

explain: 수영 종목 이름은 '평영'이고, '개구리헤엄'은 개구리처럼 팔다리를 움직이는 모습에서 나온 일상적인 말이에요. 아이들에게 가르치거나 편하게 이야기할 때 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I swim the breaststroke at the pool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헤엄이나 수영은 '치다'와 함께 쓰는 것이 가장 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Swimming words naturally go with '치다'.

phrases.en: I want to learn the breaststroke this summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수영을 배우는 이야기를 할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when talking about learning to swim.

phrases.en: I slowly went all the way using the breaststroke.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로'를 붙이면 어떤 방법으로 헤엄쳤는지 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '으로' tells which stroke you used.

explain_en: Native word for breaststroke; everyday speech, frog-like kick (저는 수영장에서 개구리헤엄을 제일 먼저 배웠어요.) The official swimming event name is '평영', while '개구리헤엄' is an everyday word based on how the arms and legs move like a frog's. It is common when teaching kids or chatting casually.

t90.ax: I moved slowly forward doing the breaststroke.

en: to open; to open to the public

examples.en: This beach opens on July 1st.
The amusement park opened at nine in the morning.

examples.ko: 스키장이 눈 때문에 일찍 개장할 거예요.
examples.en: The ski resort will open early because of the snow.

examples.ko: 새 시장이 개장하면 같이 구경 가요.
examples.en: Let's go see the new market together when it opens.

examples.ko: 개장한 지 한 달밖에 안 된 수영장이에요.
examples.en: It's a pool that has been open only a month.
There is an outdoor skating rink that opens only in winter.

explain: 해수욕장, 스키장, 시장, 놀이공원처럼 사람들이 모이는 큰 장소가 문을 열 때 써요. 가게가 하루 장사를 시작하는 건 '문을 열다'가 자연스러워요. 반대말은 '폐장하다'이고, 새로 낸 가게는 '개점하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: When is the opening day of the beach?
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 여는 날을 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing meaning the day a place opens.

phrases.en: The market is cleaned before it opens.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연결형으로 문을 열기 바로 앞의 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form for what happens just before opening.

phrases.en: The shop opens at ten.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 가게에 쓰는 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The natural everyday way to talk about a shop opening.

explain_en: Pool, beach, park or venue opens for visitors. Use it when a large public place such as a beach, ski resort, market, or amusement park opens. For a shop starting the day, 문을 열다 is more natural. The opposite is 폐장하다, and for a newly opened shop you say 개점하다.

dis.h: open a venue to the public
gh: a museum or library is opened
a school is founded and opens

p.n: Same meaning; the passive form sounds a bit more impersonal.

en: to watch a game or match as a spectator

examples.en: I watched a baseball game with a friend.
Watching Go tournaments is my hobby.

examples.ko: 경기장에서 관전할 때는 큰 소리를 내지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't make loud noises when watching in the stadium.
While watching, I paid close attention to the players' movements.
I'm going to watch the final tomorrow.
I reserved a good seat for watching in advance.

explain: 관전하다는 경기를 구경하는 일에만 쓰는 말이라 영화에는 '관람하다'를 써요. 직접 경기에 나가는 것은 '출전하다'예요. '경기를 관전하다'처럼 목적어는 보통 경기나 대국이에요.

phrases.en: I'm going to watch a soccer game this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '관전하다'에 '-(으)러 가다'를 붙여 구경하러 가는 목적을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-(으)러 가다' states the purpose of going to watch.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to watch a game

phrases.example: 이 자리에서는 경기를 가까이에서 관전할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: From this seat you can watch the game up close.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기를 볼 수 있는 자리나 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a place or situation lets you watch a match.

phrases.en: I watched a soccer game with my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 쓰는 쉬운 말이고, 경기가 아닌 것에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday word that also works for things other than games.

explain_en: Watching a game or match as a spectator. 관전하다 is only for watching a contest, so for a movie you use 관람하다. Taking part in the game yourself is 출전하다. The object is usually a game or a match, as in 경기를 관전하다.

dis.h: watch a game or match as spectator
gh: watch over patiently, see what happens

p.n: The replacement implies watching on a screen; the original means watching as a spectator.

examples.en: The farmers sang work songs while planting rice.

examples.ko: 이 노래는 옛날 어부들이 부르던 노동요예요.
examples.en: This is a work song that fishermen used to sing long ago.

examples.ko: 노동요를 틀어 놓고 청소하면 힘이 덜 들어요.
examples.en: If you put on some music while cleaning, it feels less tiring.

examples.ko: 요즘은 일할 때 듣는 음악을 노동요라고 불러요.
examples.en: These days people call the music they listen to while working a 'work song'.

examples.ko: 제 노동요 목록에는 빠른 노래가 많아요.
examples.en: My work playlist has a lot of upbeat songs.
Thanks to my work music, even boring dishwashing became fun.

explain: 원래는 일을 하면서 힘을 맞추고 지루함을 덜려고 부르던 민요를 말해요. 요즘은 청소나 공부, 일할 때 기분을 올려 주는 음악을 농담처럼 '노동요'라고 부르기도 해요.

phrases.en: My grandmother sang work songs while working in the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하며 노래한다는 원래 뜻에 가장 잘 맞는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The collocation that best fits the original meaning of singing while working.

phrases.en: I play upbeat work songs when I clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘 일할 때 듣는 음악을 말할 때는 '틀다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modern sense of music to work to goes with 틀다 (to play).

phrases.example: 친구가 공부할 때 듣는 노동요 플레이리스트를 만들어 줬어요.
phrases.en: My friend made me a work-song playlist to listen to while studying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이나 공부할 때 듣기 좋은 노래 목록을 농담처럼 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A playful name for a playlist good for working or studying.

explain_en: Originally it means a folk song sung while working to keep time and ease boredom. Nowadays people also jokingly call any music that lifts their mood while cleaning, studying or working a '노동요'.

examples.ko: 피아노 오른손 악보에는 보통 높은음자리표가 나와요.
examples.en: Right-hand piano parts usually have a treble clef.
I learned how to draw a treble clef.
Violin sheet music has a treble clef.
I can see the treble clef at the very beginning of the score.
It is hard to tell the treble clef and the bass clef apart.
My younger sibling drew a treble clef nicely.

explain: 음악 시간에 배우는 말이고, 반대는 '낮은음자리표'예요. 띄어 쓰지 않고 한 단어로 붙여 써요. 피아노 오른손 악보, 바이올린, 플루트 악보에 주로 나와요.

phrases.en: I drew a treble clef on the sheet music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악 시간에 악보를 쓸 때 자주 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often used in music class when writing music.

phrases.en: The left-hand part shows a bass clef.
phrases.nuance_ko: '높은음자리표'의 반대말이에요. 함께 묶어서 배우면 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 높은음자리표; good to learn them as a pair.

phrases.en: I can read treble clef sheet music.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악보 종류를 말할 때 뒤에 '악보'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 악보 after it to name a type of sheet music.

explain_en: You learn it in music class, and its opposite is '낮은음자리표' (bass clef). It is written as one word without spaces. It mainly appears in right-hand piano parts and in violin and flute scores.

en: to climb a mountain; to scale

examples.en: On the weekend, I climbed Seoraksan with friends.
His dream is to climb Everest.
When it snows, climbing is difficult.

examples.ko: 아침 일찍 등반하면 해돋이를 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you climb early in the morning, you can see the sunrise.

examples.ko: 등반할 때는 장갑과 튼튼한 신발이 필요해요.
examples.en: When climbing, you need gloves and sturdy shoes.

examples.ko: 산악회 사람들과 암벽을 등반해 본 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I have climbed a rock wall with people from a mountaineering club.

explain: 등산은 산에 오르는 일반적인 말이고, 등반은 바위나 높은 산처럼 힘들게 올라가는 느낌이 있어요. 그래서 동네 뒷산에는 '등산하다', 암벽이나 큰 산에는 '등반하다'를 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I go rock climbing every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '등반하다'는 바위처럼 힘든 곳을 오를 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: This verb fits well with hard climbs like rock faces.

phrases.en: I want to climb the Alps someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하고 싶은 일을 말하는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form for saying what you want to do.

phrases.en: I climbed the mountain at dawn and saw the sunrise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '등반하다'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, more everyday way to say it.

explain_en: 등산 is the general word for going up a mountain, while 등반 feels like a harder climb, as with rock or high mountains. So for a small hill near home you say 등산하다, and for rock walls or big mountains 등반하다 is more common.

en: to go up to the mound

examples.en: The ace pitcher takes the mound in today's game.
The new pitcher made his first appearance yesterday.
The president decided to step into the negotiation himself.

examples.ko: 마지막에 유명한 가수가 등판해서 분위기가 뜨거워졌어요.
examples.en: A famous singer came on at the end and the mood heated up.
Fans are waiting to see when he will take the mound.
Who is the player starting on the mound?

explain: 원래 야구에서 투수가 마운드에 올라가는 것을 말해요. 요즘은 중요한 사람이 마지막에 나설 때도 비유로 써요. '출전하다'는 모든 종목에 쓰고, '등판하다'는 주로 투수에게 써요.

phrases.en: The ace pitcher stepped up to the mound.
phrases.nuance_ko: '등판하다'와 같은 뜻을 풀어서 하는 야구 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A baseball phrase that spells out the same meaning as 등판하다.

phrases.en: That pitcher will start tomorrow's game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경기를 처음부터 맡는 투수에게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a pitcher who starts the game from the beginning.

phrases.en: That player will take part in tomorrow's game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모든 종목에 쓸 수 있는 더 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that works for every sport.
phrases.en_equiv: to take part in a match

explain_en: Originally it is a baseball word for a pitcher going up to the mound. Today it is also used figuratively when an important person steps in at the end. 출전하다 works for any sport, while 등판하다 mostly refers to pitchers.

examples.ko: 피아노를 칠 때 메트로놈을 켜 놓고 연습해요.
examples.en: When I play the piano, I practice with the metronome on.

examples.ko: 메트로놈 소리에 맞춰 천천히 쳐 보세요.
examples.en: Try playing slowly along with the metronome's sound.
My tempo keeps speeding up, so I need a metronome.

examples.ko: 선생님은 메트로놈 없이 연습하지 말라고 하세요.
examples.en: My teacher tells me not to practice without a metronome.

examples.ko: 이 메트로놈은 스마트폰 앱으로도 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: This metronome can also be used as a smartphone app.

examples.ko: 저도 모르게 메트로놈보다 조금 빠르게 치고 있었어요.
examples.en: Without realizing it, I was playing slightly faster than the metronome.

explain: 악기를 연습하며 박자를 맞출 때 쓰는 도구예요. '메트로놈을 켜다', '메트로놈에 맞추다'처럼 말해요. 요즘은 기계뿐 아니라 스마트폰 앱으로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I installed a metronome app on my phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계 대신 스마트폰으로 쓰는 메트로놈을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to a metronome used on a smartphone instead of a device.

phrases.en: Try lowering the metronome speed a bit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 메트로놈이 알려 주는 빠르기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for the speed that the metronome sets.

phrases.en: Practice was over, so I turned off the metronome.
phrases.nuance_ko: '켜다'의 반대 동작으로, 연습을 마칠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of '켜다', used when finishing practice.

explain_en: It is a tool for keeping the beat while practicing an instrument. People say '메트로놈을 켜다' (turn it on) and '메트로놈에 맞추다' (keep time with it). Besides the physical device, phone apps are widely used too.

en: kicking water; splashing water with the feet

examples.en: The kids are splashing around happily in the valley stream.
I only splashed around in the shallow part of the pool.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 여름마다 시냇가에서 물장구를 치며 놀았어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I played splashing around in the creek every summer.

examples.ko: 발로 물장구를 치면 물이 사방으로 튀어요.
examples.en: If you kick and splash with your feet, water flies everywhere.

examples.ko: 동생은 수영은 못 하고 물장구만 좋아해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling can't swim and only likes splashing about.

examples.ko: 물장구 소리가 들려서 가 봤더니 아이들이 있었어요.
examples.en: I heard splashing, so I went to look, and there were kids.

explain: 보통 '물장구를 치다'로 써요. 수영할 때 발차기와 달리 물에서 발이나 손으로 물을 치며 노는 모습에 어울려요. 주로 아이들이 노는 장면에 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: The child splashes in the bathtub.
phrases.nuance_ko: '물장구를 치다'를 붙여 쓴 동사 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A one-word verb form of 물장구를 치다.

phrases.en: We played splashing in the water at the beach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연결형으로 놀이 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form for describing playtime.

phrases.en: I can hear the splashing even inside the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물을 치는 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the sound of splashing water.

explain_en: Kicking feet in water, swimming or playing (물장구를 치다) It is usually used as '물장구를 치다'. Unlike a swimming kick, it suits playful splashing in water with your feet or hands. It mostly appears in scenes of children playing.

examples.ko: 어렸을 때 가족과 서커스를 보러 갔어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I went to see a circus with my family.

examples.ko: 서커스 단원들이 공중에서 묘기를 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The circus performers showed tricks in the air.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 서커스가 우리 동네에 와요.
examples.en: The circus is coming to our neighborhood this weekend.
The circus is popular with children.
A bear rode a bicycle at the circus show.
He is someone who used to walk the tightrope at a circus.

explain: '서커스'는 공중 묘기나 동물 쇼까지 포함한 공연 전체를 말하고, '곡예'는 그 안에서 보여 주는 몸으로 하는 재주를 말해요. 공연하는 사람들은 '서커스단'이라고 불러요.

phrases.en: A circus troupe came to our city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공연하는 사람들의 모임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the group of performers.

phrases.en: I watched a circus with the kids on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공연은 '보다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Performances pair with the verb 보다.

phrases.example: 서커스 공연이 저녁 일곱 시에 시작해요.
phrases.en: The circus show starts at seven in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공연 시간이나 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about show times or places.

explain_en: '서커스' is the whole show, including aerial acts and animal performances, while '곡예' is the physical skill performed within it. The performers are called a '서커스단'.

en: to be absorbed in; to be fascinated by; to be enthralled

examples.ko: 요즘 동생은 클래식 음악에 푹 심취해 있어요.
examples.en: These days my younger sibling is deeply absorbed in classical music.
I got absorbed in the novel and read all night.
He is someone devoted to historical research.

examples.ko: 한 가지에 심취하면 시간 가는 줄 몰라요.
examples.en: When I get absorbed in one thing, I lose track of time.
I try not to get too absorbed in dramas.
I have been fascinated by comics since I was little.

explain: 보통 '~에 심취하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 쓰고, 예술, 사상, 취미처럼 어떤 대상에 깊이 빠져 마음을 빼앗길 때 써요. '빠지다'보다 점잖고 글 같은 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 저는 요즘 한국 드라마에 푹 빠져 있어요.
phrases.en: I'm totally hooked on Korean dramas these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '심취하다'보다 편하고 말할 때 많이 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more casual expression, used a lot in speech compared with 심취하다.

phrases.en: He has been absorbed in philosophy for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊이 빠진 상태가 계속되고 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the state of being deeply absorbed is continuing.

phrases.en: The way he's absorbed in painting looks really cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무언가에 깊이 빠진 사람의 모습을 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person who is deeply immersed in something.

explain_en: Devoted to a hobby, art or idea; somewhat literary (재즈에 심취하다) It is usually used with the particle 에, as in '~에 심취하다', when you are deeply absorbed in something such as art, ideas or a hobby. It sounds more refined and written than '빠지다'.

examples.en: When the singer belted out the song on stage, the audience cheered.
My friend grabbed the mic and sang passionately at the karaoke room.

examples.ko: 열창하는 모습이 너무 멋있어서 영상을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The way he sang with passion was so cool that I recorded a video.
When my father is in a good mood, he sings trot songs with all his heart.
He is singing passionately with his eyes closed.

examples.ko: 끝까지 열창해 준 가수 덕분에 콘서트가 더 즐거웠어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the singer who sang passionately to the end, the concert was even more fun.

explain: '노래하다'와 달리 온 힘을 다해 열정적으로 부른다는 느낌이 있어요. 가수의 무대나 노래방 같은 곳에서 그런 모습을 말할 때 써요. 보통 칭찬하거나 모습을 그릴 때 어울려요.

phrases.en: The singer sang with such passion that the audience was moved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '열창'에 '하다'를 붙인 말로, 뜻은 '열창하다'와 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Noun 열창 plus 하다, same meaning as 열창하다.

phrases.en: The way he sang with passion looked really cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노래하는 사람의 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe how a singer looks while performing.

phrases.en: We sang at the top of our voices in the car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 소리로 힘껏 부를 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy phrase for singing loudly with full effort.
phrases.en_equiv: to sing at the top of one's voice

explain_en: A singer giving a heartfelt, energetic performance of a song. Unlike plain '노래하다', it carries the feeling of singing with all one's strength and passion. It is used for scenes such as a singer's stage or a karaoke room. It usually suits praise or vivid description.

examples.ko: 이 감독은 옛 이야기의 재창조로 유명해요.
examples.en: This director is famous for reinventing old stories.

examples.ko: 전통 한복의 재창조가 젊은 사람들 사이에서 인기예요.
examples.en: The reinvention of traditional hanbok is popular among young people.

examples.ko: 그 디자이너는 낡은 물건의 재창조에 관심이 많아요.
examples.en: That designer is very interested in giving old items new life.

examples.ko: 이 작품은 고전 소설의 재창조라고 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You could call this work a reinvention of a classic novel.

examples.ko: 도시의 재창조를 위해 시민들이 아이디어를 냈어요.
examples.en: Citizens offered ideas to reinvent the city.
A good translation is sometimes a recreation of the original.

explain: 있던 것을 바탕으로 새롭게 만들어 내는 것이에요. 아무것도 없는 데서 처음 만드는 '창조'와 달라요. 옛 작품이나 전통을 새롭게 만들 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: That writer reinvented the old myths.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '재창조'를 동사로 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 재창조.

phrases.example: 전통의 재창조가 요즘 큰 관심을 받아요.
phrases.en: The reinvention of tradition is getting a lot of attention these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛것을 바탕으로 새롭게 만드는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for making something new from old tradition.

phrases.en: The old song was reinvented in a new way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바뀐 결과를 말할 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Passive form describing the result.

explain_en: It means making something new on the basis of what already exists. This differs from '창조', which is creating something from nothing for the first time. It is often used for reworking old works or traditions.

en: to color; to paint in colors

examples.ko: 저는 연필 그림을 예쁜 색으로 채색해요.
examples.en: I color my pencil drawings in pretty colors.
The painter colored the mural all night yesterday.

examples.ko: 주말에 부채에 그린 꽃을 채색할 거예요.
examples.en: This weekend I'll color the flowers I drew on the fan.
Please color it after you draw the sketch.

examples.ko: 물감으로 채색한 그림이 더 부드러워 보여요.
examples.en: A picture colored with paint looks softer.
If you color slowly, the colors won't bleed.

explain: '채색하다'는 '색칠하다'보다 조금 격식 있고 작품을 만든다는 느낌이 있어요. 아이의 색칠 놀이에는 '색칠하다'가 더 자연스러워요. '~을/를 채색하다' 형태로 써요.

phrases.en: The child colors in the picture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, everyday word.

phrases.en: I hung the colored painting on the wall.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 입힌 결과물을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a finished piece that has been colored.

phrases.en: I'm coloring my artwork now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 하는 중이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you're in the middle of it.

explain_en: Artistic, coloring a drawing or painting with care. 채색하다 is a bit more formal than 색칠하다 and suggests making an artwork. For a child's coloring play, 색칠하다 sounds more natural. It is used in the form ~을/를 채색하다.

t90.ax: Please color it after you draw the sketch.
